beliefs: Every character is shifted by ASCII +1 (a→b, A→B, 0→1, space→!, ~→DEL) [E1, E5, E7]
After shifting, a lowercase letter becomes uppercase ONLY if the previous ORIGINAL character is not a lowercase letter (i.e. it is a run-start of lowercase) [E12, E13, E14, E16, E17, E18]
Uppercase letters, digits, spaces, and symbols get only the raw +1 shift with no case change (A→B, Z→[, 0→1) [E1, E2, E7, E11, E17]

The run-start test looks at the original character, not the shifted one, so 'aB'→'Bc' (B is not lowercase, so 'a' at start is uppercased) and 'Ba'→'Cb' (a follows B, not lowercase, so uppercased) [E12, E13, E16, E17]
When the run-start char is 'z', its shifted result '{' is uppercased to '[' [E8, E11, E15]
Only the first char of a lowercase run is uppercased; subsequent lowercase letters keep their raw +1 shift, so 'ab'→'Bc', 'aa'→'Bb', 'baa'→'Cbb' [E12, E13, E14, E18]
The 'z'→'[' uppercase exception applies to every run-start 'z', including 'zz'→'[{', 'zzz'→'[{{', 'zzaz'→'[{b{' [E15]
Uppercase letters are NOT lowercased after shifting; they stay as their +1 shifted uppercase/symbol (A→B, Z→[) [E7, E11, E16, E17]
notes: The only error was treating the shifted char's case as the run-state; the run-start test must use the ORIGINAL character's case (so 'a1a1a'→'B2b2b', 'aBaBa'→'Bcbcb'). Fixed predict() to track prev_lower from the original char.
